The runbook's second condition (a hosts launch not released) is covered by the same list: every job of a pending host is in it, and a launch whose hosts are all decided counts as released (settled_view), so a separate check could never fire alone (no mutant could kill it).

The runbook's row named the result's fetched SHA-256 for the cache; the run record's cache.sha256 is what hb.py reads, so the seal checks that.
